answers.answer: Separate Conflict cards by tier; shuffle all four III cards and place them at the bottom, shuffle nine II and deal five above them, then shuffle three I and deal one on top. This makes a 10-card deck (I: 1, II: 5, III: 4). Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck — 1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom. Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: Four players: start at 1 VP; three total Agents, with two on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board. Three troops start in the garrison and nine in supply; take 1 water. Three players: start at 0 VP; the same Agent, troop, and water setup.
answers.evidence: Setup: Score track ‘on the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0 space’; ‘Place two Agents on your Leader and your third Agent (your Swordmaster) next to the game board’; three troops in garrison, remaining nine in supply; ‘Take 1 water.’

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain. After revealing, you resolve Reveal-box effects only from cards just revealed, not cards played on Agent turns. Once you Reveal, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase. During Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents’ and after it ‘your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.’ Reveal Turn: effects are from ‘just-revealed cards only (not of cards played on Agent turns)’; Clean Up moves ‘all cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns) to your discard pile.’

answers.answer: No. You must pay costs immediately before resolving any effects of the space or played card, so an Agent-turn card effect cannot provide resources for that entry cost. One card can send only one Agent using one chosen Agent icon. A card without Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn; it may only be revealed on a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs ‘immediately (before resolving any effects of the space or the card you played)’; ‘You choose only one Agent icon; one card can't send multiple Agents’; a card with no Agent icons ‘may only be revealed on a Reveal turn.’

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited this turn plus up to two from the garrison, for up to five total in this case. At a non-Combat space, you do not deploy units. A troop is recruited from your supply and placed in your garrison; newly recruited troops can be deployed on a Combat-space turn.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: the cube icon takes a troop ‘from your supply and place[s] it in your garrison’; at a Combat space deploy ‘any or all units recruited during your current turn ... plus up to two more units from your garrison.’

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy, without recalling that Spy. Infiltrate lets you recall your Spy at a post connected to an occupied destination to send your Agent there anyway. Gather Intelligence lets you recall a Spy at a connected post to draw a card when sending an Agent; choose it immediately after placing the Agent and before receiving space or card effects. One Spy cannot pay for both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on the same placement, though two different Spies can be used for the two different effects.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy Agent icon permits a connected space ‘you do not recall the Spy’; Infiltrate recalls a connected Spy to ignore another player's Agent; Gather Intelligence is chosen ‘immediately after placing your Agent (before receiving any effects)’; ‘You cannot recall the same Spy to both.’

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm contributes 3, and four revealed swords contribute 4. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot participate in the Combat Intrigue window.
answers.evidence: Strength: each troop = 2, sandworm = 3, revealed sword = 1; if the last unit is removed, strength becomes 0. Combat Intrigue is available to each player with ‘at least one unit in the Conflict.’

answers.answer: Yes. Passing once does not prevent you from acting again; the window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison) and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: ‘You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; resolve once involved players ‘pass consecutively.’ Cleanup returns troops to ‘supply (not their garrison)’ and sandworms to the bank.

answers.answer: In both player counts, tied players at first each receive the second reward, and no one wins the Conflict or takes its card. With three players, no other rewards are given. With four players, if exactly two tie for first, the remaining players compete for the third reward. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first players ‘each gain the second reward, and no one wins the Conflict or takes the Conflict card’; with three or fewer players ‘no other rewards’; with four, exactly two tied means remaining players compete for third. Resolve Combat: ‘A player with 0 strength receives no reward.’

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double the rewards you take; two sandworms do not quadruple them. Taking control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice to gain 1 VP, you may pay the cost a second time to gain the reward again: 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘if you have one or more sandworms ... double’; control and battle icons cannot be doubled. Example says you may pay 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 spice for 2.

answers.answer: When you win a Conflict and take its card into your supply, check for another face-up Conflict or Objective card there with the same battle icon. If a match exists, flipping the pair is mandatory and earns 1 VP. During Endgame, you may match the wild icon with any one of the three battle icons in your supply; that match is optional and earns 1 VP when flipped.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: on winning and taking the card, check another ‘face-up Conflict or Objective card’; if present, you ‘must flip the matching pair’; ‘During the Endgame, you may match the wild battle icon with any one’ of the three icons.

answers.answer: Reaching 2 Influence gives 1 VP, which is lost if you fall below 2. Reaching 4 gives the bonus shown on that track space; you keep that bonus if you later fall below 4 and gain it again each time you climb back to 4. Tying the current Alliance holder at 4 does not steal the Alliance. If the holder later loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied player takes it; falling to 3 or lower also loses it, and if nobody has 4+ it returns to the board.
answers.evidence: Victory Points: 2 Influence = 1 VP ‘(lost if you drop back below 2)’; the 4 Influence bonus is kept and gained again on re-reaching 4. Alliance section: ‘Tying an existing holder does not steal it.’ FAQ: after holder loses Influence following a tie, the formerly tied player takes it; falling to 3 or lower loses it, returning to board if nobody has 4+.

answers.answer: Persuasion may be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool it from multiple sources for one card and split one source across different cards. The Imperium Row is replenished to five cards, so you may buy a replacement immediately if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile and are not used right away.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn permits Persuasion ‘before, between, or after’ effects. Acquiring Cards: you ‘may pool’ sources and ‘split’ a source; after replacing a Row card ‘you may acquire its replacement’; acquired card goes face up into your discard pile.

answers.answer: At a Maker space, you gain all bonus spice there. In the Makers phase, each Maker space without an Agent gets 1 spice added to its bonus spot. Maker Hooks are usually required by the sandworm icon; the token is retained when summoning. The Shield Wall prevents summoning to a Conflict at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while it remains on the board. A sandworm is summoned directly into your Conflict quadrant and can never be placed in a garrison; it can be summoned only to a Conflict not protected by the Shield Wall.
answers.evidence: Makers: an Agent-free Maker space gets 1 spice added, and an Agent gains ‘all the bonus spice there.’ Sandworms: usually require Maker Hooks, cannot be summoned to a Shield Wall-protected Conflict, and are immediately deployed to the Conflict; they ‘can never be placed in a garrison.’ FAQ: Maker Hooks ‘are retained, not spent.’

answers.answer: At the end of a round, 10 or more VP for any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then compare Victory Points. The listed tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring: ‘At the end of a round’ 10+ VP or empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame; ‘First, players may play and resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards’; tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup has 2 contracts face up and 18 face down (20 total). Add four Intrigue cards and four Imperium cards to their respective decks. Shaddam Corrino IV is an optional Leader, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix compatibility and stay in the box for standard CHOAM.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup: shuffle 20 contracts, flip two up and place the remaining 18 face down; shuffle 4 additional Intrigue and 4 Imperium cards into the decks; Shaddam is an ‘option’; 10 contrasting-back contracts ‘leave them in the box for standard CHOAM.’

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts into your supply and replace it with a contract from the bank flipped face up. If all contracts have been taken, the icon gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the stated spice amount during that turn, including spice from other sources. An Immediate contract completes as soon as taken. An Acquire The Spice Must Flow contract completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts: take one face-up contract and replace it; if all are taken, the icon reverts to 2 Solari. Completing contracts defines Harvest, Immediate, and Acquire The Spice Must Flow as stated.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a space where you already sent your Agent this turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must have held the contract when you sent the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM: if the contract involves a space where you ‘already sent your Agent this turn,’ wait until a future turn and ‘must have had the contract at the time you sent your Agent.’ On completion: announce, gain rewards, flip face down, leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the two eligible human Objectives are dealt randomly, and the First Player marker goes to the human whose card shows it. First Player alternates only between humans; each round the order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival takes Agent turns while an Agent remains in supply and never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: ‘Use one shared scoring Rival’; give it the Ornithopter Objective; First Player goes to the human whose card shows it; order is ‘First Player → Rival → other human’; ‘A Rival takes Agent turns ... and never takes a Reveal turn.’

answers.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, the Rival ignores it and reveals another Hagal card. A Place Spy card uses an empty post of its specified type, or ignores placement if none exists; either way it reveals another Hagal card because it has not sent an Agent. Ignore normal space costs and effects, applying only the revealed Hagal effects. If House Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle it and continue.
answers.evidence: Agent turns: ‘Ignore an occupied destination and reveal again’; Place Spy uses an empty specified post or ignores it, and ‘either way reveal another Hagal card’; ignore normal costs and effects. If House Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, ‘immediately reshuffle it and continue.’
